<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="תמוז_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518919310_theRebbe_548" batchId="meluket-_D7_AA_D7_9E_D7_95_D7_96_meluket__BH_POST_1766518919310_theRebbe_548__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The root of nature is from the name Elokim, while the root of miracles is from the name Havayah, with miracles either transcending nature or being clothed within it.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">5)</t>
    <t s="1">And it is known,</t>
    <t s="2">that the root of nature is from the name Elokim</t>
    <t s="3">(Elokim has the numerical value of haTeva—nature),</t>
    <t s="4">which in general is the light that fills and is invested in the worlds according to their level,</t>
    <t s="5">and the root of miracles is from the name Havayah,</t>
    <t s="6">which in general is the encompassing light that is above the worlds.</t>
    <t s="7">And from this it is understood,</t>
    <t s="8">that miracles which are not clothed in nature,</t>
    <t s="9">the root of their drawing down is from the revelation of Havayah itself,</t>
    <t s="10">which is above investment in the name Elokim,</t>
    <t s="11">and the miracles that are clothed in nature, the root of their drawing down is</t>
    <t s="12">from the revelation of the name Havayah as it is invested in the name Elokim.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This is analogous to the two levels of will in a person—will above reason and will clothed in reason—which correspond to three types of miracles.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And this can be understood by way of an analogy from the power of will in a person</t>
    <t s="1">(for will is a parable for the encompassing light),</t>
    <t s="2">which has two levels.</t>
    <t s="3">Will that is above reason,</t>
    <t s="4">and will that is clothed in reason.</t>
    <t s="5">And within this itself</t>
    <t s="6">(in the will that is clothed in reason)</t>
    <t s="7">there are two manners.</t>
    <t s="8">For even as it is clothed in reason,</t>
    <t s="9">it is revealed in it that essentially it is will</t>
    <t s="10">(which is above reason).</t>
    <t s="11">And that the will inclines the intellect in such a way that the intellect itself becomes according to the will,</t>
    <t s="12">and it is felt that what he thinks is so</t>
    <t s="13">(not because of the inclination of the will, but)</t>
    <t s="14">because of the intellect.</t>
    <t s="15">And likewise in the analogue,</t>
    <t s="16">in the revelation of the encompassing light,</t>
    <t s="17">there are correspondingly three levels as above,</t>
    <t s="18">which are the root of the three types of miracles:</t>
    <t s="19">a miracle entirely above nature,</t>
    <t s="20">a miracle clothed in nature in a way that the miracle within it is recognizable,</t>
    <t s="21">and a miracle clothed in nature in a way that nature conceals the miracle within it.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The term "miracle" (nes) means elevation, primarily in miracles clothed in nature, but even miracles above nature elevate nature through their revelation.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">6)</t>
    <t s="1">And this—that "miracle" (nes) is from the term "elevation" (haramah),</t>
    <t s="2">that through the miracle there is an elevation and ascent in nature—</t>
    <t s="3">is primarily in miracles that are clothed in nature.</t>
    <t s="4">For in miracles that are above nature,</t>
    <t s="5">the revelation of the name Havayah, which is above nature, is in a manner that nature</t>
    <t s="6">(drawn from the name Elokim)</t>
    <t s="7">is nullified by the revelation,</t>
    <t s="8">that is, the overturning of the natural order.</t>
    <t s="9">And the concept of "miracle" from the term "elevation"—that the revelation of the name Havayah is in a manner that nature</t>
    <t s="10">(drawn from the name Elokim)</t>
    <t s="11">is elevated in the light of the name Havayah—</t>
    <t s="12">is</t>
    <t s="13">(primarily)</t>
    <t s="14">in miracles that are clothed in nature.</t>
    <t s="15">Nevertheless,</t>
    <t s="16">from the fact that even miracles that are not clothed in nature are called by the name "miracle" from the term "elevation,"</t>
    <t s="17">it is understood</t>
    <t s="18">that also through these miracles there is an elevation and ascent in nature.</t>
    <t s="19">For since</t>
    <t s="20">the overturning of nature through the miracle is only in one particular aspect and not in the entirety of the matter</t>
    <t s="21">[as in the miracle of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds,</t>
    <t s="22">where the change</t>
    <t s="23">(the overturning of nature)</t>
    <t s="24">was only in that the water stood up like a heap and like a wall,</t>
    <t s="25">but the essential substance of the water remained as it was before],</t>
    <t s="26">it follows,</t>
    <t s="27">that even in these miracles,</t>
    <t s="28">the revelation of the name Havayah is in investment in the nature of the entirety of the thing in which the miracle occurred,</t>
    <t s="29">and through this there is an elevation and ascent in it.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
